title: Fixed Bored Boss Cymbal Pair and Whole Link Cord
description: One newly authored complete static tingsha-inspired small cymbal pair, counted together with its whole joining cord as one independent instrument prop. Each whole thick plain metal-look cymbal has a returned finite outer rim, sloping face, raised central dome with a real bounded centre bore, and an open underside cavity rather than a filled disc. One entire curved cord travels from a fixed end-knot appearance beneath the first dome, through its bore, across the gap, and through the second bore to its whole fixed end-knot appearance. The bores remain wider than the narrow cord and both rims have finite planar resting annuli. All numeric radial profiles, complete cord path and end forms are new, not a drum-kit cymbal extracted from its stand or a tambourine jingle pair with its hoop removed. Unlike the drum kit, there is no tripod, clamp cap or drum; unlike the tambourine, there are no shared pin-captured jingle windows or supporting wood hoop. The autonomous whole two-boss and bore-to-bore cord organization is newly authored together. Five closed editable whole meshes, four opaque constant PBR roles, metres native Z up and complete horizontal bounds-centred ground origin. One model zero scenes. Broad instrument-category inspiration only, without copied ornament, inscriptions, a named artisan, historical replica, religious performance, luck, health or spiritual-efficacy claims. The plain enlarged cord ends indicate fixed knot appearances, not reconstructed working knot topology; internal overlaps only establish visual attachment. No acoustic response, pitch, ringing duration, striking simulation, cord flexibility or tension, gravity equilibrium, actual metal/leather identification, fit, manufacture, safe handling, rigging, animation or interaction supplied or verified.
